title: Clean-by-construction: a documented from-scratch run yields a DB needing no cleanup
description:
GOAL: anyone running the extraction passes as documented in CLAUDE.md, starting from an empty DB, must end up with a database that requires no manual cleanup.

This separates two kinds of work we've been conflating:
- REACTIVE (clean the current mixed Haiku+DeepSeek DB, one-time): building_domain-4se (purge IFC junk), building_domain-cst (purge pre-scope activity constraints), building_domain-o8f (re-run skipped pass 10). A from-scratch run would not reproduce these EXACT states, so they are historical fixes, not goal items -- except where they reveal a recurring generator (below).
- PREVENTIVE (fix the pipeline + docs so junk never gets created): the real goal. Each recurring junk generator needs a pipeline fix and CLAUDE.md must document the clean procedure.

KNOWN GENERATORS and preventive-fix status:
1. LLM-invented IFC class names/prose pseudo-classes -> building_domain-y30 (seed ifc_class from schema). PREVENTIVE EXISTS.
2. Quota-padded / duplicated patterns (DeepSeek returns ~8) -> building_domain-8tk (quality/dedup prompt). PREVENTIVE EXISTS.
3. Pass 5 unbounded inline activity creation (19k activities) -> NEW bead. GAP.
4. Pass 10 global-progress resume silently skips new data across runs -> NEW bead (promoted from o8f 'deeper fix'). GAP.
5. Scoping pass 6/7 to non-activity entities -> already fixed in code (building_domain-zu4, closed) and must be reflected in CLAUDE.md.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) every generator above has a merged pipeline fix; (b) CLAUDE.md's documented extract command + procedure reproduces a clean DB from scratch (correct model, scoped passes, schema-seeded IFC, no manual SQL afterwards); (c) a from-scratch smoke run on a small seed produces zero hallucinated ifc_class rows, no quota-padding artefacts, and a fully-normalized graph.
notes: Raised 2026-06-24 from user goal. P1 because it governs whether the project is reproducible by others. See bd memory 'goal-a-documented-from-scratch-run-of-the'.

title: Re-run pass 10 (10a/b/c) against DeepSeek data — normalization was skipped
description:
Pass 10 sub-passes 10a (ref resolution), 10b (predicate stabilization), and 10c all SKIPPED during the DeepSeek extraction run because their global pass_progress records ((sub,'__global__',embedding_model)) were already 'completed' from an earlier Haiku-era run (10a/10b on 2026-05-26, 10c on 2026-06-03), and bsos extract calls run_normalize(reembed=False) which does not clear them.

CONSEQUENCE: none of the data produced by this run's passes 4-9 was normalized. Confirmed: all 46,743 deepseek-chat patterns have force_ids=[] AND related_pattern_ids=[] (100% unresolved). New pass-6 predicates were not stabilized either. The graph is missing its entire normalization layer for the new data.

FIX (run after the extraction finishes):
  sqlite3 bsos.db "DELETE FROM pass_progress WHERE entity_id='__global__' AND pass_number IN ('10a','10b','10c');"
  bsos extract --passes 10 --models deepseek-chat   # --models needed for 10b LLM disambiguation
Do NOT use --reembed (deletes all embeddings, requires threshold recalibration).

CAVEAT TO VERIFY: 10a resolves refs via embedding similarity, so new entities/forces/patterns must have embeddings to match against. If 10a reports many pending/unresolved refs, the new items lack embeddings and a targeted re-embed may be required first. Watch 10a output.

DEEPER FIX (separate): run_normalize should detect when new un-normalized data exists since the last 10a/b/c completion and not silently skip -- the global-progress resume is unsafe across multiple extraction runs that add data.
notes: Raised 2026-06-24 mid-run (pass 11). User correctly identified that 10a/b/c ran before the deepseek resume. P1 because the new knowledge is unusable for force/pattern graph queries until normalized. Related: building_domain-8tk (pattern dedup, also pass-10-adjacent via related_pattern_ids).

title: MCP tool: entity discovery / semantic search
description:
An IFC-manipulating agent receives element names and types from ifc_info (e.g. IfcSpace Name='Entrance Hall') and needs to query bsos — but bsos requires an exact entity name. There is no tool that maps from an IFC element description to relevant bsos entities. Without this, the agent must guess entity names and the whole query chain is fragile.

Add a bsos MCP tool (e.g. search_entities) that accepts a free-text description or IFC class name and returns ranked matching bsos entities. Semantic similarity (embedding-based) is the right approach given entity names may not literally match IFC names. This is the bridge between the two systems and is the most critical gap for agent usability.

title: abstraction_node_effective_origins SQLite view
description:
Create the required SQLite view abstraction_node_effective_origins (Section 4.8, Section 12).

The view computes majority knowledge_origin for AbstractionNode records via GROUP BY + aggregation over child assertions. Required because any query filtering or sorting AbstractionNode by knowledge_origin MUST join against this view — it cannot be bypassed by call sites.

bsos init MUST create this view alongside Alembic-managed tables. bsos doctor MUST verify its existence and fail loudly if missing.

SQL sketch:
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS abstraction_node_effective_origins AS
  SELECT an.id AS node_id,
         a.knowledge_origin,
         COUNT(*) AS origin_count
  FROM abstraction_nodes an
  JOIN assertions a ON a.id IN (json_each(an.assertion_ids))
  GROUP BY an.id, a.knowledge_origin;

description:

title: Pass 10 normalization must not silently skip when new un-normalized data exists
description:
run_normalize keys 10a/10b/10c resume on GLOBAL pass_progress records ((sub,'__global__',embedding_model)). Once completed, a later 'bsos extract' (reembed=False) skips them entirely even if passes 4-9 have since added thousands of un-normalized rows. This is exactly what bit the DeepSeek run (building_domain-o8f): 46,743 patterns left with empty force_ids/related_pattern_ids. A multi-stage or resumed from-scratch run hits the same trap.

PREVENTIVE fix for epic building_domain-27w: make normalization detect outstanding un-normalized data rather than trusting a single global 'completed' flag. Options: track a high-water mark (e.g. max created_at processed) per sub-pass and re-run on anything newer; or invalidate the global completion when new assertions/patterns/forces are written after it; or scope 10a/b/c progress per extraction batch instead of one '__global__' record. Outcome: running the documented passes end-to-end always normalizes everything, with no manual DELETE-from-pass_progress step (which o8f currently requires).
notes: Raised 2026-06-24. Promoted from the 'DEEPER FIX' note in building_domain-o8f (which stays as the one-time data fix for the current DB). Generator #4 in epic 27w.

Added embedding-free detectors per pass; made 10c incremental (dedup against existing AbstractionNode child_ids) and fixed 10b phase1 to rewrite reintroduced mapped predicates. CLI run_normalize uses the same detectors. New regression tests assert new data after completion is normalized while clean re-runs still skip. title: Bound/control Pass 5 inline activity creation (19k activities from one run)
description:
Pass 5 (_get_or_create_activity) mints a new activity EntityRow for any predecessor/successor name the LLM returns that doesn't already exist, with no bound. In the DeepSeek run this exploded the graph from ~9.9k to 26.9k entities (19,213 activities), inflated passes 6/7 (forcing the zu4 scoping), and drove the lock contention in building_domain-cc0. A from-scratch run would reproduce this.

This is a PREVENTIVE item for the clean-by-construction epic (building_domain-27w): decide what the correct behaviour is and enforce it. Options to evaluate: (a) only create an activity if it matches/normalises to an existing entity, else record as a pending ref rather than minting (mirrors how other passes handle unresolved object names); (b) cap/curate inline activities against a seed activity taxonomy; (c) mark inline-created activities with a distinct status/source so they are clearly second-class and excluded from passes where they add noise. Whatever is chosen, the result must be that a documented from-scratch run does not balloon the graph with thousands of unvetted micro-activities.
notes:
EVIDENCE-BASED REASSESSMENT (2026-06-26, after the full DeepSeek run): recommend NOT implementing the Pass 5 bound as framed; it would destroy value. Inspected the 19,213 activities: the overwhelming majority are legitimate construction-sequencing activities (Electrical Rough-In, Window Waterproofing/Flashing Installation, Formwork & Reinforcement Placement, Drainage/Stormwater Pipe Installation, Final Commissioning) — i.e. exactly the knowledge BSOS exists to capture. 19,061 of 19,213 (99.2%) participate in >=1 process_relation, so they are load-bearing sequencing nodes, not phantom noise.

The downstream harms originally cited are already neutralised: passes 6/7 were scoped off activities (zu4) and the stale pre-scope activity constraints were deleted (cst, done 2026-06-25). Lock contention (cc0) is a perf concern, not data quality.

The ONLY real noise is domain DRIFT: a small minority (~114 matched on furniture/object keywords; order hundreds at most) are object-manufacturing activities (Paintbrush Assembly, Seat Cushion Foam Molding, Cut Headboard Lumber, Compost Pile Formation). Root cause is the ENTITY BOOTSTRAP including non-building objects (chairs, paintbrushes, paintbrushes), not Pass 5. RECOMMENDATION: re-scope this issue (or supersede) to 'entity bootstrap should not seed non-building objects' and keep Pass 5's get_or_create behaviour. Graph size alone is not a defect.

title: Seed ifc_class entities from the authoritative IFC schema; stop LLM-bootstrapping IFC classes
description:
ROOT-CAUSE fix for the recurring IFC junk that building_domain-4se cleans up reactively. Today ifc_class entities are invented by the LLM (Pass 1 bootstrap and Pass 12), which produces hallucinated class names ('IfcHydronicHeatingSystem', 'IfcHotel') and prose pseudo-classes ('IFC Mechanical Equipment', 'IFC Flow Distribution System', 'IFC Animal Facility Space'). The ifc_class table is 682 rows of mixed valid/invalid. Purging after the fact (4se) has to be repeated after every extraction because the LLM keeps re-inventing names from training data.

PROPOSAL: make the ifc_class layer canonical-by-construction. Seed it deterministically from the IFC schema instead of from the LLM:
- Enumerate valid IFC entity/type names from the schema via ifcopenshell (ifcopenshell.ifcopenshell_wrapper.schema_by_name('IFC4'/'IFC4X3').declarations()) or the ifc MCP server's ifc_schema tool. Cover the schema version(s) the project targets (IFC4 minimum; _test.ifc is IFC4).
- Create one ifc_class EntityRow per real IFC entity with the canonical name (and ideally the schema description/supertype as metadata), marked with a deterministic source (e.g. source_model='ifc-schema') so they are distinguishable and never purged by 4se.
- Stop Pass 1/Pass 12 from minting new ifc_class entities by free-text: either drop ifc_class from the LLM concept-discovery output, or constrain Pass 12 to map only to the pre-seeded canonical set (reject/abstain when no real class matches, rather than inventing one).

OUTCOME: ifc_class entities always correspond to real IFC types; get_ifc_psets and scripts/ifc_compliance_report.py get a reliable mapping target; 4se becomes a one-time historical cleanup rather than a recurring chore.
notes:
LANDED 2026-06-27 (commit 6068cbe): deterministic seeder + pipeline guards.
- bsos seed-ifc-classes: enumerates 776 IFC4 entity classes via ifcopenshell (src/bsos/persistence/ifc_schema_seed.py), writes one ifc_class EntityRow each (source_model='ifc-schema', status='accepted'). Idempotent; adopts an exact-name LLM entity in place. --schema IFC4X3 -> 888.
- Pass 1 drops LLM-minted ifc_class concepts; Pass 12 maps only onto seeded set (_resolve_ifc_class), skips unknown classes instead of minting.
- CLAUDE.md updated to seed before extract. Tests: tests/integration/test_seed_ifc_classes.py (6). Full suite 511 passed.

STILL OPEN (the original NOTES blocker): adopt-in-place only folds EXACT-name matches into a seed. Valid prose variants that do NOT exactly match a canonical name (e.g. 596 valid prose ifc_class entities -> 359 canonical) still need a real merge that repoints constraints.subject_id, antipatterns.subject_id, forces/spatial_relations/process_relations FKs (pass2._merge_cluster only repoints assertions). Tracked in new follow-up. Also: run seed + dedup against the production bsos.db (current cleanup, not pipeline).

title: Prompts elicit quota-padded output (DeepSeek returns exactly 8 patterns); add quality-over-quantity guidance
description:
Pass 8 writes exactly 8 patterns for the overwhelming majority of entities (live DB: 884 entities with exactly 8 patterns vs 27 with 3-7). This is not a code/schema cap -- PatternExtractionResponse.patterns is an unbounded list and the prompt requests no count. It is DeepSeek V3's output bias: given an open-ended 'list the patterns' prompt with a per-item schema, it settles on a round number (8). The result is patterns padded to an implicit quota rather than a count reflecting how many genuinely apply -- e.g. a Wet Pipe Sprinkler System getting 8 'Alexander-style spatial patterns' when few real ones exist. Quality is uneven; several per entity are likely filler.

The same open-ended 'list all X' framing exists in pass 6 (constraints), pass 7 (anti-patterns), and pass 9 (forces) and very likely produces the same quota-padding there. Worth checking each distribution.

CHANGE: add explicit quality-over-quantity guidance to the pass 6/7/8/9 prompt templates, e.g. 'Only include items that genuinely and specifically apply to this entity. Quality matters far more than quantity -- it is correct to return few items, or none, when the entity is not rich in this dimension. Do not pad the list to reach a count.'

CAVEATS: (1) prompt change busts the LLM cache for the affected pass (new prompt = new cache key) -> re-extraction cost on re-run; (2) only affects not-yet-processed entities, so this is a next-run improvement, not a hot-swap into the current job. Sequence it for after the current run, or for a clean re-run of the affected passes.
notes: REFINED FRAMING (2026-06-22, after inspecting Wet Pipe Sprinkler System's 8 patterns): the quota-padding does NOT produce garbage -- the patterns are genuine, specific, NFPA-flavored design patterns. The padding manifests as REDUNDANCY: when the model runs out of distinct patterns it SUBDIVIDES one into variants to reach 8. Concrete example: 'Grid-Integrated Sprinkler Head Layout', 'Sprinkler Head Alignment with Architectural Grid', and 'Concealed Piping above Accessible Ceiling' are essentially one pattern (coordinate sprinkler heads with the ceiling/structural grid) split three ways. So the real win of the prompt change is DEDUPLICATION, not 'fewer bad patterns'. Prompt guidance should explicitly say: do not split a single pattern into near-duplicate variants to reach a count; merge overlapping patterns into one. Also note: pass 9's related_pattern_ids resolution may already flag some of these as near-duplicates -- check whether that pass can be leveraged to collapse them post-hoc instead of (or in addition to) the prompt change. Original evidence (884 entities at exactly 8) still stands.
close_reason: Added shared QUALITY_GUIDANCE (in bsos.pipeline.__init__) appended to pass 6/7/8/9 prompt templates: instructs models to include only genuinely-applicable items, return few/none when appropriate, and not split one item into near-duplicate variants. Committed 531e775. 458 tests pass. Caveat (already noted): prompt change busts the per-pass LLM cache, so it only affects a future re-extraction, not the current DB's already-processed entities.

title: Scope passes 6 & 7 to non-activity entities (skip the 14k inline activities)

title: Purge hallucinated IFC class names from the entity graph
description:
The ifc_class entities contain hallucinated IFC type names that do not exist in any IFC schema. Confirmed example: 'IfcHydronicHeatingSystem' (no such IFC entity). Others are clearly invented too, e.g. 'IFC Class: IfcHotel' (no IfcHotel). The names are also malformed/inconsistent: some are bare ('IfcHydronicHeatingSystem'), some wrapped in prose ('IFC Class: IfcBoiler', 'IFC Beam (IfcBeam)', 'IFC Class IfcDoor (Shop Entrance)'). 390 ifc_class entities total (status != merged), many invalid.

TASK:
1. Build the authoritative list of valid IFC entity/type names. Source it from the IFC schema rather than the LLM — e.g. ifcopenshell (ifcopenshell.ifcopenshell_wrapper.schema_by_name('IFC4'/'IFC4X3').declarations()) or the ifc MCP server's ifc_schema tool. Cover the schema version(s) the project targets (IFC4 at minimum; the test model _test.ifc is IFC4).
2. For each ifc_class entity: extract the candidate Ifc* token from the (often prose-wrapped) name and check it against the valid set, case-sensitively on the canonical IFC capitalisation.
3. Purge or quarantine the hallucinated ones: delete the entity rows AND their dependent assertions/constraints/spatial_relations/process_relations, or set status to a new 'invalid'/'rejected' value so they are excluded from MCP queries. Decide delete vs quarantine (quarantine is safer/auditable).
4. Normalise the surviving valid ones to canonical names (strip the 'IFC Class:' prose wrappers) so they match real IFC class names exactly — this is what get_ifc_psets and the compliance report rely on.

WHY: BSOS maps bsos entities to IFC (get_ifc_psets, scripts/ifc_compliance_report.py). Hallucinated IFC class names break that mapping and mislead any agent that trusts them as real IFC types.
notes:
PARTIAL DONE (2026-06-25, post-DeepSeek run): Built authoritative valid set from ifcopenshell IFC4+IFC4X3 declarations (1173+1311 names). title: Re-paraphrase APL pattern prose for shipped bsos.db
description:
The patterns table in bsos.db is populated by bsos curate apl-import, which copies problem/solution text verbatim from data/apl_patterns.json. That JSON was itself LLM-generated from A Pattern Language (Alexander, Ishikawa, Silverstein, 1977) — so the database contains second-hand paraphrases, not book text. However a paraphrase can still be a derivative work, and we want the shipped bsos.db to be clearly redistributable under ODbL.

## Fix

Add a pipeline step (or extend bsos curate apl-import) that runs the problem/solution text through one further round of LLM paraphrasing before writing it into the patterns table. The pattern names, numbers, ids, confidence ratings, and higher/lower pattern graph are factual and stay unchanged. Only the prose fields (problem, solution) need re-generating.

The re-paraphrase should:
- Preserve the meaning and intent of each pattern accurately (patterns are central to the tool)
- Be clearly the tool's own expression, not traceable to the book's wording
- Use claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 for cost efficiency (same as the extraction pipeline)

## Result

The shipped bsos.db contains no text derived from the book, only:
- Pattern names / ids / graph (fair use / factual)
- LLM-generated prose created by this tool's own pipeline
- LLM-generated assertions from passes 1-12

This allows bsos.db to be licensed under ODbL 1.0 with attribution notices (tracked separately).

- Edge types — assertion edges: requires/depends_on/protects_from/unsuitable_for/improves/conflicts_with/contains/connects_to/supports

title: bsos compress command: semantic compression (Section 9)
description:
Implement bsos compress CLI command (Section 17 compress spec + Section 9).

Command: bsos compress [--min-cluster-size N] [--dry-run]

Steps:
1. Group accepted/proposed assertions by subject_id. Embed texts (all-mpnet-base-v2), cluster semantically similar ones. Only clusters ≥ min-cluster-size (default 3) proceed.
2. For each qualifying cluster: LLM-A synthesis call — 'what single statement captures all of these without introducing new information?'
3. LLM-B adversarial validation: 'does this abstraction assert anything not already present in these source assertions?' If LLM-B unavailable or same model as LLM-A: skip validation, set status='proposed', emit structlog warning about single-model abstraction.
4. Create AbstractionNode (status='proposed', child_ids, abstraction_rationale). Store to abstraction_nodes table.

Queue cap check: if proposed AbstractionNode count ≥ 200, exit with message pointing to bsos review-pending --type abstraction. --dry-run bypasses this check.

--dry-run: run clustering and synthesis, print candidate abstractions and child counts, do NOT write AbstractionNode records.

LLM provider: default_llm_model for synthesis (LLM-A), constraint_validation_model for adversarial validation (LLM-B), falling back to default_llm_model with warning.

Pass dependency: requires at least one assertion with status IN ('accepted', 'proposed').

Note: bsos compress is distinct from Pass 10c (abstraction synthesis in the extract pipeline). compress is operator-triggered; Pass 10c is part of normalize. They share the same core algorithm but compress is a standalone command.

title: Conflict detection batch: bsos validate --conflicts
description:
Implement the deferred conflict detection batch (Sections 10.1, 10.2, 10.3).

bsos validate --conflicts [--limit N]

Three sub-tasks in sequence:

1. Assertion/constraint/pattern conflict detection (Section 10.1):
   - Process all proposed items where conflict_evaluated_at IS NULL
   - Embedding similarity pre-filter (all-mpnet-base-v2), then LLM classification: duplicate|complementary|contradictory|unrelated
   - Before classification: check conflict_pairs for existing row — skip re-classification if found, apply status update directly
   - For contradictory pairs: write to conflict_pairs table, set status='conflicted' on both items, write provenance_log rows
   - Set conflict_evaluated_at = now() on each evaluated item
   - Conflict queue cap: when >500 conflicted items, pause status transitions (still write conflict_pairs rows), emit warning on bsos extract/normalize/validate invocations
   - --limit N: stop after N LLM classification calls

2. ProcessRelation divergence detection (Section 10.2):
   - For each (predecessor_id, successor_id) pair with rows from ≥2 distinct source_model values
   - Check hard_constraint consistency — if any two rows disagree: mark all rows for that pair as conflicted, write conflict_pairs, write ReviewDecision(decision='defer')
   - Display disagreeing models and hard_constraint values in review queue

3. Process graph cycle detection (Section 10.1 validate spec):
   - Find strongly connected components of size ≥2 in the full ProcessRelation graph
   - Mark all ProcessRelation edges in cycles as status='conflicted', add to review queue

4. AbstractionNode cascade (Section 10.3):
   - When any item's status changes to conflicted or deprecated, re-evaluate parent AbstractionNodes
   - Query: abstraction_nodes WHERE json_each(child_ids).value = <child_id>
   - Apply cascade rules per Section 10.3

Output: summary of items evaluated, conflicts found, auto-promoted, ProcessRelation divergences flagged, cycles detected.

title: Entity bootstrap seeds non-building objects, causing activity domain drift
description:

TASK: constrain the Pass 1 concept-discovery prompt (and/or a post-filter) so it does not emit furnishable/manufacturable objects as first-class building entities — or scope them so Pass 5 does not generate their manufacturing sequences. Preventive item for the clean-by-construction epic (building_domain-27w). Measure the drift precisely first (keyword + LLM classification) before deciding delete vs prevent.
notes:
PREVENTIVE FIX LANDED (fa02c1c, 2026-06-26): added SCOPE_NOTE to all three Pass 1 concept-discovery prompts (BOOTSTRAP, DOMAIN, EXPANSION). Keeps building fabric/systems/spaces/materials + fixed/building-integrated FF&E (IfcFurniture is legitimately modelled); excludes loose consumer goods, personal/gardening/composting items, tableware, toys; and restricts activities to on-site construction/installation/commissioning, never off-site manufacture. 458 tests pass. A broad keyword sweep (chair/seat/bench/bed/table/desk/etc.) over component/material/system entities is dominated by false positives — building fabric ('Mortar Bed','Bed Joint','Chair Rail','Road Bed','Window Seat','Lamp Post') and building-integrated FF&E ('Auditorium Seat','Grandstand Seating','Reception Desk') that IFC models. title: Pass 5+ writers occasionally hit 'database is locked' under 2 workers
description:
During long DeepSeek extraction runs, pass5 (and likely passes 4/6-9 with the same pattern) occasionally log 'pass5_entity_error ... (sqlite3.OperationalError) database is locked' when inserting an inline activity entity (_get_or_create_activity -> session.flush, pass5.py:79).

ROOT CAUSE: WAL allows one writer at a time. Each _process_entity holds the write lock across many ops in a single transaction (flush per new activity + dedup SELECT + flush per relation). With 2 workers contending plus occasional WAL checkpoint stalls, a blocked writer can exceed the 30s busy_timeout (database.py:32) and error.

IMPACT: benign + recoverable. The exception fires before session.commit() (pass5.py:198), so the transaction rolls back and no PassProgressRow(status=completed) is written -> the entity is reprocessed free (LLM cached) on the next run. No corruption, no data loss. Re-running the same extract command backfills skipped entities at no API cost.

POSSIBLE FIXES (pick one, all low-risk): (1) retry the per-entity transaction on OperationalError 'database is locked' with short backoff; (2) shorten the write-transaction hold time by committing inline activity creation in its own short transaction before the relation loop; (3) raise busy_timeout to 60000. Option 1 or 2 preferred over just bumping the timeout.

description:
Add a concrete LLMProvider implementation for local models via Ollama (PROPOSAL.md Section 2, Phase 2 requirement).

The LLMProvider protocol is already defined (extract() and classify() methods). Phase 1 has an OpenAI-compatible provider. Phase 2 requires an Ollama fallback path.

Implementation:
- OllamaProvider class in bsos/providers/ollama.py implementing LLMProvider protocol
- Uses ollama Python client (or direct HTTP to localhost:11434)
- Structured output: use instructor with ollama backend, or use Ollama's native JSON mode if instructor doesn't support it
- extract(prompt, schema, *, entity_name) → BaseModel: POST to Ollama with schema as JSON mode constraint
- classify(prompt, options) → str: simple prompt to select from options list
- model_id property returns the Ollama model name (e.g. 'llama3.2', 'mistral')
- Retry logic: wrap all calls with exponential backoff (3 attempts, 1s initial, 2.0x, max 60s) per Section 6.2
- Timeout: respect llm_timeout_seconds config key (default 120s)
- CLI integration: bsos extract --models ollama/llama3.2 should route to OllamaProvider (detect 'ollama/' prefix in model id, or use 'ollama' as provider keyword)
- Config: document how to set default_llm_model to an Ollama model

Tests: unit tests with mock HTTP responses (or skip if Ollama not running — mark with pytest.mark.requires_ollama); at minimum test that OllamaProvider implements the LLMProvider protocol and that retry logic fires on simulated failure.

Pass 3 complete. 9934 entities, 22,548 assertions. Plural/singular normalisation fix added 1031 assertions that were previously dropped. Passes 4-12 deferred pending funding.

Entity origins: 9,896 entities from LLM bootstrap prompt (single call asking for 'all major building concepts in a typical building', then expanded into sub-concepts per top-level concept). 253 entities from APL pattern names seeded via --seed-apl. The knowledge is LLM-synthesised from training data — no external documents are ingested. The bootstrap is biased towards standard commercial/residential construction; domain-specific gaps (hospital, data centre, industrial, heritage, climate-specific, site/infrastructure) are tracked in building_domain-59h and child issues.

Next: demo work — bd ready shows building_domain-1ko (normalize), building_domain-8ii (build-graph), building_domain-ki3 (Alexander analysis), building_domain-euf (MCP demo), building_domain-jhg (re-paraphrase APL patterns).

RESOLVED 2026-06-27 (building_domain-61y). The 274MB monolithic data/bsos_snapshot.json was split into per-table files under data/snapshot/<table>.json (entities, assertions, constraints, patterns, forces, antipatterns, spatial_relations, process_relations, abstraction_nodes), each <100MB (largest antipatterns 93.6MB on disk / 89MB packed). The 295MB blob was purged from the 11 un-pushed commits via git filter-branch over origin/main..HEAD, and main was pushed (7f14a29). bsos import now accepts a directory of per-table files OR a single combined .json; bsos export writes per-table files when given a directory target (trailing slash). README + .gitignore updated; the monolith is gitignored. GitHub warns antipatterns/patterns exceed the 50MB *recommended* size but accepts them (100MB hard limit). If a future raw run pushes antipatterns past 100MB, shard that table or run cleanup first.

We have summaries of all 253 patterns from Christopher Alexander's A Pattern Language. These can be used to: (1) seed Pass 1 extraction with pattern names as building concepts, (2) populate ground-truth Pattern records via bsos curate (Section 16.1), (3) populate tests/fixtures/pattern_critique_cases.json for the pattern critique test (Section 16.4). Tracked in building_domain-4a6 (ground truth ingestion) and building_domain-gv3 (Pass 1 seeding).

The compliance capability now exists at two altitudes. (1) MCP tool: bsos validate_element(entity, facts) in src/bsos/mcp_server/server.py — the agent-facing path. An agent extracts model facts via the ifc MCP server (floor_materials, window_count, door_count, systems_present, has_insulation), passes them in, and gets structured per-constraint pass/fail/unchecked instead of judging prose itself. (2) Script: scripts/ifc_compliance_report.py — a human report and demo client. BOTH share one deterministic engine, src/bsos/validation.py (classify_constraint/evaluate/validate_constraints/antipattern_signals/antipattern_triggered), so they can't diverge. Engine is pure/IFC-agnostic/DB-free. Unmatched rules + all must_not prohibitions return typed UNCHECKED detail='no_deterministic_matcher' — the slot a future LLM-assisted pass fills (em3 design decision: deterministic now, LLM fallback later). The report (i5b) also checks spatial adjacency (shared bounding walls) and antipatterns (negative-signal detection); those remain script-side, not yet in validate_element which is constraints-only. On _test.ifc: 76 checks 33 PASS/36 FAIL/7 UNCHECKED. Closed: i5b, em3.

Pass 10a/b/c normalization no longer trusts the bare __global__ 'completed' pass_progress flag (building_domain-5ut fix). Each pass module now has a cheap, embedding-free has_outstanding_work(engine) detector; the skip gate is 'completed AND not has_outstanding_work'. 10a: any PatternRow with non-empty force_descriptions/related_pattern_names (cleared to [] when resolved). 10b: any distinct non-core assertion predicate not yet in pending_predicates; also fixed phase1 already-mapped branch to rewrite reintroduced predicates. 10c: any subject with >=min_cluster_size assertions having an id not in any AbstractionNode.child_ids; made incremental via _covered_assertion_ids (skips fully-covered subjects and clusters, no duplicate nodes). cli/normalize.py uses the same detectors. This removes the manual 'DELETE FROM pass_progress' workaround that o8f/the DeepSeek run needed.

As of the full DeepSeek 12-pass run (2026-06-25), the knowledge tables are now POPULATED (previously all empty): constraints 85,817; antipatterns/failure_modes 69,464; spatial_relations 13,274; forces 45,263; patterns 46,996; process_relations 24,239; assertions 22,866. The compliance report can now check dimensional constraints, failure anti-patterns, and adjacency rules, not just requires/depends_on. Caveats from this run: entities ballooned to 27,400 — 19,213 are 'activity' entities from runaway Pass 5 inline creation (building_domain-yms); ifc_class entities (688) contain hallucinated/invalid names (building_domain-4se); patterns are quota-padded (building_domain-8tk); 1,641 Pass-3 entities have phantom progress records but no assertions.

GOAL: a documented from-scratch run of the extraction passes must produce a clean database that needs NO post-hoc cleanup. Implication for triage: distinguish reactive cleanup of the CURRENT (mixed Haiku+DeepSeek) DB from preventive pipeline/doc fixes. Prefer preventive fixes -- every recurring junk generator must be fixed in the pipeline (and CLAUDE.md must document the clean procedure), so that cleanup beads become one-time historical fixes, not per-run chores. Tracked by the 'clean-by-construction' epic.
